topic.angle: Seeing faces that are not there

body.claim: Your brain can find a face where there isn't one.
body.why: Pareidolia is the tendency for perception to impose a meaningful interpretation on a nebulous stimulus, usually visual, so that one detects an object, pattern, or meaning where there is none. Common examples include seeing faces in inanimate objects and the Man in the Moon. Face pareidolia has also been demonstrated in rhesus macaques.
